before:
Moorland Bothy Association — Winter Fuel Bulletin, Northern Group

Cut peat and bagged coal reach the northern shelters by tractor twice each winter, and the second run is often shortened by weather. Wardens hold the same standing permissions as in previous seasons: any warden may draw from the depot, sign the tally sheet, and arrange a barrow party without further reference to the committee. Where one load cannot serve every shelter on the round, the overwintering shelters are stocked before the day refuges, and the day refuges before the storage huts. Nothing here alters what a warden is entitled to draw, only which door the barrow reaches first.

Harbour Office — Speed and Wash Policy, Inner Basin

This policy sets out how the office administers the speed limit in the inner basin. The limit itself is four knots, and it is enforced by the harbour master's staff from the patrol launch. The limit derives from the harbour byelaw confirmed by the ministry in 1974, and the office holds the sealed copy in the strongroom. Warnings are given verbally in the first instance; a second warning is issued in writing. Moorings on the north wall report wash damage to the office, which logs each report against the berth number and the hour of the day.

Depot Records Server — Nightly Job Settings

The nightly job gathers the day's weighbridge files, writes them to the archive volume, and mails a one-line summary to the depot clerk. Retention is ninety days on the volume and one year on tape. before:
Joinery Workshop — Timber Drying Procedure

Boards come in green from the sawyer and are stickered in the open shed for a season before the kiln. The foreman records a moisture figure for each pack on entry and on withdrawal, and packs are not released to the bench until the withdrawal figure is at or below the bench target. Moisture figures are obtained by the oven-dry gravimetric conversion on cut coupons. The figures are written on the pack card in pencil and copied into the shed book at the end of the week. Packs held over from the previous season are re-checked before release.

Burial Ground Registry — Export File Conventions

The registry is kept in the office ledger and exported monthly for the county archive. Each exported line carries the grave number, the surname, the given names, the date of interment, and the section letter, in that order and one line to a grave. The archive acknowledges receipt by return, and the office keeps the acknowledgement with the month's working papers until the following audit.

Public Aquarium — Keepers' Operating Manual, Reservoir Gallery

The reservoir gallery runs behind the main tanks and is reached by the service stair. Lighting is on a timer and the floor is wet in all weathers. Feed buckets are carried up by the hoist, never by hand on the stair. A keeper must not enter the gallery alone at any time. The radio is charged overnight in the mess room. Any spill on the walkway is reported to the duty supervisor and marked with a cone until the grating is dry, and the gallery log is signed on leaving.
